label: frontier • draft a .docx brief, then revise it in place twice with file_edit (no regenerate), verify by reading back
query: Draft a one-page project brief as brief.docx with a title 'Atlas Migration Brief' and three headed sections: Goal, Scope and Timeline, each with two or three bullet points; the first Timeline bullet must be 'Kickoff: April 7'. Then make two revisions to the file you just wrote, editing it in place with file_edit rather than rewriting it: (1) change the kickoff date to May 5, and (2) add a fourth section headed Risks with two bullet points after Timeline. Finally read brief.docx back and tell me the final section headings in order.
notes: Drafting workflow: one file_write to create the document, then in-place file_edit revisions on the generated .docx (paragraph replace for the date; append/insert_paragraph or a multi-paragraph replace for the new section), then a verification read. The audit forbids a second file_write so the revisions must go through the document editor, and the checker confirms the final text order Goal < Scope < Timeline < Risks, the revised date, and that the old date is gone. Budgets leave room for todo bookkeeping (a planning-tool call between steps is normal on a multi-step task).

commands.command: python3 -c "import zipfile,re; x=zipfile.ZipFile('brief.docx').read('word/document.xml').decode(); paras=[''.join(re.findall(r'<w:t[^>]*>([^<]*)</w:t>', p)) for p in re.findall(r'<w:p[ >].*?</w:p>', x, re.S)]; text='\n'.join(paras); assert 'Atlas Migration Brief' in text, text; assert 'May 5' in text and 'April 7' not in text, text; idx=[next(i for i,p in enumerate(paras) if p.strip().rstrip(':').lower()==h) for h in ('goal','scope','timeline','risks')]; assert idx==sorted(idx), (idx, paras); assert sum(1 for p in paras[idx[3]+1:] if p.strip()) >= 2, paras[idx[3]:]"

rubric: The final answer lists the brief's section headings in order: Goal, Scope, Timeline, Risks.
